title: 🛰️ Four Companies from Three Countries on a Single Rocket — India Launches a New Space Partnership!
body: 🛰️ Four Companies from Three Countries on a Single Rocket — India Launches a New Space Partnership!

Indian space company Skyroot announced a partnership bringing together four companies from three countries on the second orbital flight of its Vikram-1 rocket. The partnership was announced on November 19 during the European space technologies expo in the German city of Bremen, and includes Hex20 from India, Exolaunch from Germany, and Ohm Space from Italy, in addition to Skyroot itself.

The rocket carries two small CubeSat satellites: the first, Nila 3, built by Hex20, and the second, Scope, built by Skyroot itself — both four standard units in size. Exolaunch will provide the satellite deployer and manage, integrate, and launch the mission, while Ohm Space tests aboard Nila 3 a small electric thruster that works by heating, used to raise and stabilize the orbit and deorbit the satellite at the end of its life.

Nila 3 was originally booked on one of SpaceX's rideshare flights, before moving to Vikram-1 — a vote of confidence in the Indian rocket after its first successful orbital flight on July 18, 2026. No launch date has been announced yet, with some reports pointing to 2027.

The rocket is about 20 meters tall, consists of four stages, and carries about 350 kg to low Earth orbit. With the success of its first flight, India became the third country in the world, after the United States and China, to possess a private orbital launch capability.

Simply put: imagine a small rocket carrying satellites for three countries, pushed by companies of four different nationalities — that is how the space industry has become global cooperation, not just a national race.
Are you amazed that small startup companies now launch rockets into space?
